newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Andacollo copper mine to start up Nov.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Andacollo copper mine to start up Nov.

text.p: Canada Tungsten's Andacollo copper mine in northern Chile will start producing copper this month and is expected to come fully operational in the first quarter of next year, said a project official.
"We hope to produce minor amounts of copper in November," project general manager Britt Reid told Reuters.
The pit is small by Chilean standards with annual output of 20,000 tonnes.
Reid said the mine has been crushing and storing mineral for the last 2-3 months in preparation for startup.
The mine, which cost $84 million to build, will produce copper using low-cost heap-leaching technology.
Canada Tungsten owns 63 percent of the mine, with Chile's Compaa Minera del Pacifico holding 27 percent and 10 percent held by state mining company Enami.
